title: ID P0-1: bank account name is resolved by the server

requirements.expectation: One server helper resolves bank code + account number to a holder name and returns resolved, not_found or unavailable. The existing resolve-account route uses it and keeps its response shape and its per-user rate limit for signed-in callers.
requirements.verification: Unit tests for the three outcomes, a missing key and a provider timeout; existing route behaviour unchanged.
evidence: src/lib/server/payments/resolve-account.ts; src/app/api/payments/resolve-account/route.ts now wraps it (signed-in rate limit unchanged; auth is now optional, see resolve-anonymous; an unreachable bank now returns 503 instead of 400)
src/lib/server/payments/__tests__/resolve-account.test.ts: resolved, not_found, provider error, network failure, 401/403/429, missing key

requirements.expectation: POST /api/payments/resolve-account works without a session so the signup bank step can show the bank's name. Anonymous callers are limited to 10 lookups per 10 minutes per client IP, get 429 with Retry-After over budget, and get 503 (no bank call) if the limiter is unavailable. Signed-in callers keep 20 per minute per user.
requirements.verification: Route tests for anonymous success, 429, limiter-unavailable 503 and the signed-in budget; a local run against the dev server.
evidence: src/app/api/payments/resolve-account/route.ts; src/app/api/payments/resolve-account/__tests__/route.test.ts
Local dev server, 2026-11-14: 12 anonymous POSTs from one forwarded IP returned 10 provider answers then 429 twice. Not run on the hosted environment.

requirements.expectation: Signup stores the resolved name for motorist and Repair Pro rows. A client-sent bankAccountName never reaches the database.
requirements.verification: Route tests: a typed name that differs from the resolved name is not stored; the resolved name and bank_account_resolved_at are.
evidence: src/lib/server/signup/preflight.ts resolveSignupBank; src/app/api/auth/signup/route.ts; src/lib/server/signup/pro-profile.ts writes bank_account_resolved_at
src/lib/server/signup/__tests__/resolve-signup-bank.test.ts. Tested at the helper, not through the full signup route. Motorist signup writes no bank columns, so only the Repair Pro row is affected.

requirements.expectation: When the resolver is unavailable, signup succeeds with bank_account_name null and bank_account_resolved_at null. When the bank reports no such account, signup is rejected before any account is created.
requirements.verification: Route tests for both outcomes; no auth user created on not_found.
evidence: src/lib/server/signup/__tests__/resolve-signup-bank.test.ts: unreachable bank continues with no name; unknown account returns 422 before createOrAttachUser is reached (ordering by code inspection of the route, not a route test)

requirements.expectation: POST /api/profile/update stores the resolved name on first-time bank setup, behaves like signup when the resolver is unavailable, and ignores a name-only patch. The existing destination-change gate still rejects a different account without proof.
requirements.verification: Route tests: name-only patch leaves the stored name unchanged; first-time setup stores the resolved name; existing gate tests pass.
evidence: src/lib/server/payments/bank-save.ts planBankNameColumns; src/app/api/profile/update/route.ts

src/lib/server/payments/__tests__/bank-save.test.ts; src/app/api/security/__tests__/change-bank-journey.test.ts (name-only save, unchanged-account save, first-time setup resolved / unknown / unreachable); existing gate tests pass

requirements.expectation: change_bank stores the resolved name. If the resolver is unavailable or the account is not found, the request fails and the previous bank row is unchanged.
requirements.verification: Route tests for resolved, not_found and unavailable; previous row asserted byte-for-byte on the failures. Existing change-bank journey test passes.
evidence: src/app/api/security/action/route.ts change_bank

src/app/api/security/__tests__/change-bank-journey.test.ts: typed name discarded; unreachable and network failure return 503 with both role rows unchanged and the proof still usable; unknown account returns 422

requirements.expectation: The BVN/NIN bank-account name comparison uses the resolved name. With no resolved name it is unknown, never match. Resolving later recomputes it without a new ID provider call.
requirements.verification: Tests: typed name equal to the ID holder but resolved name different yields mismatch; unresolved yields unknown; late resolve updates gov_id_meta.
evidence: src/lib/server/identity/bank-name-match.ts; signup passes the resolved name into checkSignupIds

resolve-signup-bank.test.ts: typed BVN-holder name with a different bank name yields mismatch; unresolved yields unknown. bank-save.test.ts: late resolve rewrites gov_id_meta. Not changed: POST /api/verify/pro-id still passes the stored bank_account_name, which may be a legacy typed name until that account is next confirmed.

requirements.expectation: Escrow payout, cashout and refund bank loaders return a bank only when it is resolved. An unresolved row is resolved at that point and stored; on failure no transfer is attempted and funds stay where they are. beneficiary_name is always the resolved name.
requirements.verification: Loader tests for resolved, legacy-unresolved-then-resolves and legacy-unresolved-fails; payout tests show no provider transfer call on failure.
evidence: src/lib/server/payments/bank-save.ts confirmedBankName; src/lib/server/payments/bank-lookup.ts; src/lib/server/security/cashout-engine.ts getBankOnFile
bank-save.test.ts and bank-lookup.test.ts. No new test drives payout-settlement or the cashout engine end to end; getBankOnFile has no direct test.

requirements.expectation: The cross-role bank sync copies the resolved name and resolved-at together, and payout_methods.verified reflects whether the name is resolved.
requirements.verification: Sync tests for resolved and unresolved sources.
evidence: src/lib/server/identity/identity-sync.ts

src/lib/server/identity/__tests__/identity-sync.test.ts: confirmed name and stamp mirrored, payout_methods.verified true; typed name never verified. change_bank does not call the sync, as before, so payout_methods is refreshed on the next sync.

requirements.expectation: The account name field in the bank forms is display-only with no visual change. The admin bank endpoint returns nameResolvedAt.
requirements.verification: Component tests for the two bank forms; admin route test. Manual check of both forms against docs/UI.md.
evidence: use-bank-details-fields.ts exposes nameFromBank; the three name inputs are read-only once the bank has answered and stay editable when the lookup fails. src/components/profile/security/bank-change-flow.tsx is unchanged: it still has a typed name field, which the server discards.
src/app/api/admin/pros/[id]/bank/route.ts returns nameResolvedAt. No new component or admin route tests; existing component tests pass. Manual UI check not run.

requirements.expectation: Local development without a Flutterwave key can still complete mock payouts through an explicit stand-in that cannot be reached in production.
requirements.verification: Test that the stand-in is refused when NODE_ENV is production or a real key is set.
evidence: resolve-account.test.ts: accepted only with no key on a non-production runtime; refused in production and preview; ignored when a key is set

requirements.expectation: No protected file is edited; fee, split, timer and payout formulas are unchanged; touched files stay at or under 300 lines.
requirements.verification: Diff review against docs/RULES.md section 10; full test suite, lint and typecheck.
evidence: No protected file edited. Full suite 2464 tests, typecheck and lint pass locally. Files already over 300 lines grew slightly: profile/update/route.ts +9, security/action/route.ts +20, identity-sync.ts +9.

requirements.expectation: The migration is applied on the hosted database and existing rows read as unresolved.
requirements.verification: Hosted schema check and a row count of resolved versus unresolved; no personal data in evidence.

requirements.expectation: On the hosted environment a real account resolves at signup and bank change, and a legacy account resolves at its next payout.
requirements.verification: Timestamped hosted run for each path; account details masked.

code: ID P0-5: show the name mismatch on the Care review screen and stop approval over it.
POST /api/verify/pro-id: confirm the bank name before comparing, or record unknown for a legacy name.
Tests still missing: full signup route, getBankOnFile, admin bank route, bank form components.
bank-change-flow.tsx: replace the typed name field with the bank's answer.
Optional one-off backfill so legacy accounts are confirmed before their next payout.
external: Apply migration 085 on the hosted database BEFORE deploying this code; the code reads and writes bank_account_resolved_at.
Confirm the live Flutterwave key resolves real accounts on signup, bank change and a legacy payout.
Monitor payouts held with 'Repair Pro bank incomplete' after release: these are legacy accounts the bank could not confirm.
